ques: This may be a dumb question (as in there may be a glaringly obvious answer that I'm overlooking)... but is there a way to calculate the square root of a number without having a calculator or other device with a square root button? Like, how would you figure out the square root of a number using only +,-,×, and/or ÷?
answ: what i would do, for example, to find the square root of 7, is guess and check and keep narrowing the window. 2 squared is 4, and 3 squared is 9. so it's between 2 and 3. multiply by 100 to make it easier. 20 squared is 400, 30 squared is 900. so the square root of 700 is between 20 and 30. .....25 squared is 625...... so it's more than 25. ... 26 squared is 676. ....the difference between those last 2 results is 51, so i know it's gonna be 53 up to the next (27 squared = 729). ok so it seems like 26.5 is gonna be pretty close to the square root of 700. add more digits and say what's 265 squared, i mean that's a little heavy perhaps to do in your head, but you said you're allowed to use "+,-,×, and/or ÷", so, 265 squared is ... (260x260 + 5x5 + 260x5x2) which is (67600 + 25 + 2600) which is 70225. so that's...... fairly close. this means 2.65 squared is 7.0225. maybe we can check 264 squared -- just take the previous result and subtract 264 and 265. so 70225 minus 529 is 69696. so that means 2.64 squared is 6.9696. it looks like the answer is about half way in between the two previous results. so 2.645 is getting closer still. if you want to keep narrowing it down, you'd have to add more digits, and check 2645 squared, and see which side of 7000000 it's on, then check the one on the other side, and do the same thing again. but we've got it down to approximately 2.645, without a calculator

ques: i want to learn romanian, should i go down the youtube route or duolingo?
answ: this is the method i recommend: find genuine conversational content in the language, with accurate transcriptions. this can be harder to find for more obscure languages, but that is what you need. auto-transcribe is usually not quite good enough to be reliable, so it's better to get something that has been truly and accurately transcribed by a real person. genuine conversational content, by real native speakers (not made-up textbook scenarios, you need real people really talking naturally). then run the transcript through a translator and then just start getting curious about what means what. let your curiosity drive you. maybe even start fixing the mistakes of the transcription. after a few weeks you can start guessing the translation based on the written transcript, and then, after a few months, you can start trying to transcribe just based on the audio alone. in addition to this, continue listening/watching the content casually in your free time. and most importantly, be patient. this will take years. it doesn't take skill, it takes time and curiosity. don't worry about speaking. just keep spending more and more time listening and breaking down what you're hearing, listening, listening more, and eventually after a few years the language will automatically start spilling out of your mouth

ques: Does the circle of 5ths serve a purpose other than being a tool to help people memorize what notes are sharp/flat in a key signature?

I guess it visually shows the relationships between different key sigs (which is cool), but not sure if I understand the practical use of it when it comes to actually playing music?

I think if you want to learn how to play in a certain key, you kind of need to build up that muscle memory of what it 'feels like' for your hands to be playing in that key. Knowing that A major has a C#, F# and G# doesn't mean you can just freely/easily play in A major on the spot (if you're not already comfortable playing in that key). I guess the circle helps you quickly figure out what notes are in the key, but I can only see that being helpful in a practice situation... And if you're just practicing, you can just, like... look up the notes of the scale on the internet...
answ: it's a tool to make your keyboard not sound like crap. but the work has already been done. you don't need to worry about it. your keyboard is already tuned to 12-tone-equal-tempered (which is what makes the keys all wrap around neatly like that), so the work has already been done. enjoy your keyboard sounding like not-crap in every key

the graphic is just telling about a cool pattern. it's something you'd probably notice by yourself anyway if no one had told you. it's like when someone tells you the last digit of multiples of 9 gets one lower each time. neat. the numbers still work fine regardless of whether you know about that, or whether or not you think it's neat

ques: I saw this form of musical notation in a question asked to you on August 14, 2018: "3/4 3..45./2...../1..23./lo7...../lo6.lo7.1./lo5...3./4..321/2...../ 3..45./2...../1..23./lo7...3./4.3.1./1...lo7./1.1235/8.1.../"; you mentioned in your answer that this is a form of notation you use as well when you only have access to text to write music. It looks interesting and efficient, but I can't make heads or tails of it. Would you mind explaining this form of notation, to a musician-in-training who's used to standard music notation?
answ: this person's notation system is very clear to me. they did a good job presenting all the necessary melodic information, specifically the pitch and the rhythm. they are using numbers for scale degrees, so for example in the key of C that would be 1=C, 2=D, etc. They've indicated the rhythm clearly making every note the same length, and using dots do fill equal sized spaces with no notes. The slashes are clearly barlines. thanks to their time-signature hint at the top (3/4) we can assume that each digit or dot represents an eighth note of time. Also very useful is that they are distinguishing notes in different octaves by saying "lo7" to represent the 7 below the 1, and so on. So the melody is represented quite clearly and precisely. Information that is NOT included here: chords, tempo, and note duration. However, this particular melody is so strong and familiar the chords are just about totally obvious

ques: Any tips for learning a new language?
answ: the way i approach a brand new language is this: find some videos of people having real conversations (not scripted) like podcasts or something like that. the more you enjoy the content, the better. but you also need it to have a reliable human-made transcript. then get the transcript translated. then just start getting curious about which sounds mean what, and go from there. listening is king, but the transcript will unlock what you're hearing. a crucial important tip is do NOT expect yourself to 'remember' or 'memorize' anything. that's just not how it works. with more and more and more and more and more exposure, whilst being curious, the brain will do what it does naturally, which is learn. your brain is much better at learning than you will ever understand. trust that this will happen naturally with enough exposure and curiosity. the only other thing that may throw you off is how ridiclulously long it takes

This is likely more common than I think, but that's not the main point I want to make. A common thing I tell myself is that "learning music theory will help me actually make something" and then at that point I have to wonder; how much theory should I actually know?

I don't want to sound like any other artist, neither do I want to be trapped into one genre. Self expression is important in art, and I feel as if an arbitrary concept will hold back at that (especially with something as highly regarded as music "theory"). However, I also feel as if being completely clueless about it won't lead to any progress.

probably the majority of musicians nowadays go straight to sound, without having any intermediary silent paper stage. the silent paper thing can be fun, but it's a specific thrill that does not need to be the default way, and probably is only possible if you have sufficient experiencing making audible music

ques: do you find creative ideas to be better or more valuable when they come out of nowhere versus when you make yourself come up with them? i find myself doing both but the former tends to be wayy more creatively fulfilling/cathartic although it happens super rarely, while the latter is a way more reliable way of making things for me but i often find myself not caring nearly as much about it if i do it that way
answ: no need to discriminate. you can have both, you can do both, you can use both. there are advantages and disadvantages to each. the free gifted ones have the advantage of having a mythical quality to them and sometimes they are way deeper and more genuine sounding, but the disadvantage of course is that you have no control over when you get them, and also sometimes they're kind of bland or maybe even just something that already belongs to someone else. But for your idea-gen sessions, while it may seem like you could never get that same sparkle, the tip i have for getting the most out of the idea-gen is just do a lot. do A LOT. try to make the first 12 bad on purpose. Once you loosen up, you'll forget you're doing this and it will be essentially just like you're dreaming while you're awake, once the pressure is off. Also, ...... here's the other thing, when you do a lot of idea-gen all day, it will actually loosen you up so that when you take a break, or maybe in bed tonight or tomorrow, you'll find that you'll be suddenly receiving more of the rando gifts than you otherwise would. so it's a win-win. beyond that, just add them all to the same club and later down the line you'll find there's no need to discriminate between which ideas came from which methods. there's other methods too by the way

ques: You've mentioned in the past how your work process has 3 roles in it, the idea-creator, the idea-chooser and the idea-finisher.

I wanna hear how you think the chooser works, cause oftentimes I find myself with loads of different cool ideas that I want to realize, and what ends up happening is that I get a bunch of unfinished scraps which I don't have the motivation to finish, or which I'm frustatingly unable to figure out how to complete. How does the chooser pick the best ideas so that the creator doesn't get bogged in unhelpful unfinished projects?
answ: it's more roles than that, but that may have been in context of someone's specific question about their own process

there's no need for the list to bog you down. the list is a well of opportunity. When you the 'procucer' decides "it's time to produce something", the 'selector' then goes into the list, and, by some method, makes a selection, and hands the selection to the producer. And then the producer produces that selection, and the selector does not make a selection until the producer has produced the previous selection. So the only burden, is basically what the selector selects. and yes it's a lot of pressure on the selector to make a selection that everyone is happy about, but there's no need for the LIST to be a burden. it's just the selection that's the burden. but of course it's not a burden, because the fun fact here is that any idea can be worked good. In either case, whether or not you love the selection, your motivation for following through on it might often be the sheer excitement of what you can produce next. i think the power of this method probably comes from a firm agreement you have in the scheduling department to simply continue to produce things diligently one after another, as a coping strategy for the overwhelming potential at stake

ques: In your answer to someone asking whether or not you liked imaginary numbers, your answer was: ' i do now, ever since i started thinking of positivity and negativity as a full circle instead of just binary' Could you elaborate? I hold a linier view of positivity and negativity.
answ: think of positive 1. on the right side of the number line. it's totally positive, always positive. 1 times 1 equals 1. Now think of negative 1, on the left side of the number line. always negative. Negative 1 times negative 1 equals positive 1 (the negatives cancel out). but imagine that these two points (left and right, negative and positive) are actually part of a circle that goes all the way around. 1 straight up would be a number called "i" in mathematics. imagine that this number can't decide whether it's positive or negative. it's half positive half negative. So what's i times i? 'i' can't decide whether it's positive or negative, so you take one of each. like 1 times -1. the result is negative 1. And this is of course exactly the definition of i, it's the square root of negative 1. Directly straight down would be negative i, which of course also squares to negative one because like the upper i, it also can't decide whether it's positive or negative so you also get one of each, except technically in the opposite order

ques: Could you elaborate on the music and non-music thing. it seems to come up a lot in your answers but I'm not sure what you mean.

For example: a song featured in a movie. You usually like the song better when it's in the movie, and it also makes the movie better to have the song in it. Another example: background music in a movie-- the music is the music, and the non-music would be the dialogue and what's happening in the scene. the music is there to make the scene stronger (hopefully). Another example: Joey Your-favorite-artist, singing a song. the music would be the music, and the non-music would be the words and ideas being expressed, or even the identity and personna of the artist, to whom you may feel a special connection. Another example: an instrumental song by Ricardo the Really Good Xylophone player. even if there's no words in the song, the non-musical element here is Ricardo himself and perhaps the crazy hat he's wearing, on the album cover, which you probably can't help thinking about when you listen to the music. Ok so now you may ask me this: What if you are going shopping in a store and you hear the same xylophone song, WITHOUT knowing who the artist is or seeing his crazy hat. you're probably thinking, "aha, here's a situation where it's just the music and no non-music" NOT TRUE, the non-music here is obviously YOU SHOPPING, which when combined with the song creates an unforgettable shopping experience

ques: If you were gonna say no, But changed your mind to say yes when you thought about it. What did you reaally think about that would turn your initial answer around to then abswer the opposite. What was your thought proccess?
answ: let's look at some examples. someone said "Why do you think people started building things? Maybe Boredom?" my first instinct was no, this is absolutely not the reason for building. building things is because you want to do a lot of things that you can't do because you don't have the tools to do it. so you need to build things to help accomplish what you need to. 'boredom' seems like a very wrong way to describe the root cause. but then i was trying to figure out what is the cause behind wanting to do more complex things than were ever possible before. and it became harder to deny that 'boredom' COULD be a way to describe this, even though i'd probably prefer to use a word like 'curiosity'. i suppose it could be argued you could be curious about the future while being bored of the past. so ultimately i couldn't really disagree with the person's initial suggestion Let's look at another example: someone said "do you love satiation". at first i just didn't recognize the word. so i probably would lean toward no. then i did some surface level research and also remembered the word "insatiable", which is a word i like to use, especially while rubbing my fingers together to comminicate the concept of an unquenchible desire. and this led me to the conclusion of heck yeah i'd love to be satiated Let's look at just one more example, because "where there's 2, there's more" Someone said "Have you ever had a fever where the only prescription was more cowbell?" my first instinct was, this is not a question, this is a quote, from a famous saturday night live sketch starring christopher walken. therefore the person asking this here is not really asking what this is asking, they're just repeating a quote. and so to stay grounded in these situations i often use the cold hard truth as a go-to. my instinct was to say no, because i have so much to say about what it means and what it takes to really assemble music arrangements, it just felt initially so unlikely that this bit would actually ring true. But after thinking about it for a moment, it suddenly occured to me that this happens all the time. in the course of music production, it is absolutely not at all uncommon to find yourself deeply hankering for a cowbell at certain choice junctures

ques: In perfect the characters mention several times they are going to go somewhere else but they never do. Was there originally a plan to have the characters go somewhere else or was it always the intention to have the characters remain in one place?

That means at each moment when i'm writing the story, i have just as no idea what's going to happen next as you the first-time viewer. i could rave through the ceiling trying to explain all the advantages i find in doing it this way. most importantly it ensurees that the writer and viewer are always in the same space. but anyway, this video in particular is a celebration of the no-outline method, so it's plan-free. are they going somewhere? they certainly can, the option is always open, so that's probably why the possibility comes up from time to time. you can be sure that any time someone asks if they are going somewhere, i the writer did not know the answer yet at that time

ques: oh my gosh i just have to share this with you: i was working on a video and i was debating 16:9 and 3:4, and took note of the common resolution number 1440. then i was synchronizing an animation to music and needed something to spin at 180 degrees every ~4 frames to be a 16th note in length per revolution - and needed it to spin for eight (8) 16ths notes which let me to this same number i was working with earlier when calculating: [total rotation needed for 180 degrees/16th over eight (8) 16th's] or 8 * 180 = 1440(degrees) and i was quite taken aback upon reading that from the calculator. and now i wonder why resolutions use these circular numbers and also why do circles. couldnt # of degrees per 1 rotation be based on any number besides 360? wait is it a CIRCLES RESOLUTION? im glad you were here for this unplanned epiphany thanks for being someone to talk about this to
answ: the reason 360 is a good number for a circle is because it divides well. you can divide by 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6 and still have a whole number. very useful. screen resolutions probably also have usefulness in being well dividable, for example if you want to display something at half size, or a third size. 1440 can also be neatly divided by 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6. so it's not the hugeset coincidence that you ran into 1440 twice in this process.

ques: i've been guitaring and whatnot for a couple years now and i got the idea to make a shitty little EP just cause i want to play music and get music out there. i have a tendency to procrastinate indefinitely if i'm not actually making steps towards something. but 15 minutes of trying to figure out how you record stuff has totally zapped me of any desire to do it. even like, buying mics, i don't know what a compressor is. it's an entire new skillset (and money sink) i wasn't prepared for. penny for your thoughts
answ: yes i give this thought all the time. at the risk of boring some people to death who always hear me give the same advice, i will say that the feeling you are having is exactly what happens when you start too big. now you may be saying 'but wait, i didnt think i was starting that big', well, too bad, it's still too big for you at this moment. and so youve been knocked on the ground. The answer to this is extremely simple, and it's just to start smaller. For example, you say 'i dont know what a compressor is.' Ok, great. then dont use it right now. Honestly, it's a huge shame that you have even heard of a 'compressor' right now, because all it's doing for you is bringing you some sense of 'obligation' to do something youve never even identified, never consciously needed or wanted, means nothing to you at this time. which is precisely why you had no energy to think about it. So anyway, back to a mic, because yes you do want make music that can be stored in a bottle and played back at a different time (i believe that was your original desire.) This is a lot like going up a staircase. when you approach the stairs for the first time, are you saying "Which step SHOULD i go to? which is the best and most professional step, to step on?" and then you get overwhelmed and pass out into a depressed nap. but what you should have asked instead is ARE ANY OF THE STEPS STEPPABLE, FROM THE GROUND. are any of the steps right next to the ground where i can step on it. the answer is yes and that would of course be step number 1 for you. Anyway, back to mics, dont buy a mic, the golden rule to start, is of course 'use the one you already have.' Yes, if you really dont have any microphone device, then go to the nearest store and buy any mic, but the thing is i'm sure you actually do already have a microphone device. almost any device that can type something into this question box probably has a mic on it. in contrast to that horrible dreadful feeling of confusion and guilt, i think you may find that the idea of starting your musical journey using only whatever's already right there with you on your deserted island, is just absolutely romantic. you can take your pet volley ball along

ques: when you finish writing a song but haven't yet recorded it, to which degree do you know how it's going to sound like, compared to when it's fully finalized? have you ever ended up with a wildly different result than what you were expecting while writing?

ques: I was in a language learning Discord server at some point, and someone brought up a really interesting practice method. First some context. Suppose person A speaks French and wants to learn English, and the reverse for person B. Sometimes these people get together for "language exchange", which in this case is having a conversation in French, and then the next will be in English, and they'd alternate like this at whatever frequency A and B agree upon. The problem is that people who engage in this practice are usually not yet familiar enough with the language to make non-trivial sentences themselves, which greatly limits how complex the conversations can get. So it's hard and somewhat boring. The idea is that since these people need more input in their target language, they should just have conversations where A speaks French and B replies in English. They both get natural input in their respective target languages, without being limited in what they want to say. This sounds great on paper, so I'd like to convince the entire universe to try it to see how well it holds up in practice. How would I go about this?
answ: i already know that's a great method. and it sounds like you suspect it also. of course what i would suggest is not to go trying to convince the entire universe of something. if it's good, the universe will probably find out anyway. and if it's not, then they'll be pretty mad at you for trying to force this on them

ques: What are some of your ideas catching techniques? For instance, say a song idea comes to me while I'm in the car or when I'm already rushing to get ready in the morning (which is when most of my song ideas come to me of course)
answ: if you have no immediate way to write it down, start analyzing it in non-musical ways to remember the data. for example: quiz yourself about how many notes it has. quiz yourself about what tempo value it has. count the words. make up acronyms that match the first letters of the words. list out the note values. quiz yourself on how many 8th rests there are. these are basically just to familiarize yourself with the data from all angles, and it serves to just help you remember the information. also you can pretend you are dictating it to someone else to write down, who has no knowledge of music notation. so imagine you have to explain to them how to transcribe all the deetails. all these tricks should help you remember the correct original information accurately without it being carelessly mixed up with something else equally musical or plausible

ques: when you try to find the prime factors while waiting in a line, are you doing this in your head???? how do you even go about doing that?????
answ: yes i do it in my head, it's a casual empire of skill i've been quietly building over the past 15 years or so. to tell you every trick and technique might take 15 years, but, for example, let's say the number is 166747. i could tell you how to tell it's not divisible by 2, but you probably already know how to do that. i could tell you how to tell it's not divisible by 3, but, they probably already taught that one to you in school. i could tell you how to tell it's not divisible by 5, but you probably already know that also. they tend to teach you in school there's not really any trick to checking anything higher, so i will tell you how to check 7 (or anything). manipulate it by adding or subtracting multiples of 7 until you shrink it enough to recognize it. level it off to a zero at the end and drop the zero, because dividing by 10 never changes its 7-status. you can also divide by 2 if it ever becomes even, if you feel like it. 166747 --> 16674 ---> 1666 ---> 161. i already recognize it there, but if not then you'd subtract 21 and get 14. which you probably recognize. but then again, i'm not really sure where other people are at on this, because i've been thinking about numbers all my life. i'm perfectly familiar with 14 as a multiple of 7, but i have no idea if this is general common knowledge to other people. 1001, 501, 301, 203, 323, 216, 1024, all those numbers are just as familiar to me as 14, just because of how long i've been doing this, but i have no idea how far others have gone on this. so that's why i was able to stop when i hit 161, because i already recognize that as 23x7, and to get there i readily used 7, 14, and 56. this was me trying to give a short answer, are you proud of me

ques: I think it's interesting how the medium influences how music is written and presented. Like, pre-recorded music you had pieces of all sorts of lengths because there was no need to "fit" a piece of music onto a radio or record. Then with recordings you had a very pretermined "quantity" of music you can fit on there .. you started seeing the famous 3-5min long song for radio and 45's/singles, and maybe a full album, cassette or CD you can have somewhere around 30-45min of music. I think it's weird though that in the digital age, not much has changed since the early days of recorded music. With less people buying hard copies of music and internet/streaming becoming more common than radio...The digital age is more similar to the pre-recorded days in that you can have a piece of music last however long you want since you dont need to fit it into a physical medium... and yet, we still see a majority of songs (at least popular songs) fitting in that 3-5min range and albums (though not as popular as they once were, with many artists putting out singles instead of albums) are still typically in that 30-45min range when an artist does put out an album. Do you think streaming and stuff like that just hasn't been around long enough yet for popular music to start taking more liberties with song/album durations? ques: I've sometimes heard other self-employed artists who make content for YouTube say that while they love their jobs, one thing that they kind of miss from having a "normal" job is that it makes it easier to have a good work-life balance-if you work a 9-to-5, in most cases, you have a certain amount of time in the day when you're on the clock, at the office (or wherever you work), working; but once your shift is over, you have time left over in the day to do other non-work-related activities, and go to bed at a fairly consistent time every day-therefore the day is clearly separated into time when you're working, and time when you aren't. But when you're your own boss and work from home or in a studio, there's not that same clear separation between time for working and time for doing other things, so it's easy to get so caught up in the work you're doing-because you're passionate about it-that it occupies the large majority of your day, which isn't inherently a bad thing, but that can lead to not having much time for anything else-such as going outside, hanging out with friends, or even sleeping-which can have long-term negative effects on your relationships and health. Can you relate to these struggles in any way? Do you have any advice for self-employed artists having difficulty maintaining a good work-life balance?

ques: Hey bill. I can write a chorus but I have a hard time writing a verse. My verse melodies feel like filler. I want the verse to be as good as the chorus. Not sure what good means. Should the verse be catchy like the chorus? Hasn't worked thus far. Should I approach the verse differently?
answ: first of all, it's almost impossible to write backwards. if you have a 'chorus' but you need something to come before it and you dont have it yet, it's almost impossible to find it, you kind of have to get lucky. BUT, a wise real estate agent once told me, "dont make the verse too good, you wanna save that for the chorus". And i wanted to disagree with him at the time, but i do believe that strategy should lead you to constructive places. Actually here's something i always almost forget to suggest: Just run the chorus and see what you wanna do after the chorus. then just continue from there. and if your chorus is good enough, chances are you'll end up leading back to it again. Then, take that part after the chorus, and start your song there with some alternate lyrics and it should lead to the chorus just fine. BUT, all this babble about 'verse' and 'chorus', it makes me want to give a reminder: the duck expert who thought all animals had beaks never discovered any of nature's wonderful beakless offerings. sorry for answering this question 4 times at once, but you can see i have a lot to say on this

ques: do you think some people have a more natural inclination towards creativity (in any medium) that is at least a little bit innate? as someone whose education path and hobbies leaned heavily towards "maths/computers" and other stereotypically "logical" stuff i found myself drawn to, i have long realised that i don't find any of that deeply fulfilling but worry i have too much of a stereotypically "left-brain" to actually have any unique or interesting creative expression. then again i realise this way of overthinking it is probably part of the issue. i do have very specific tastes and know exactly what i would want to do, but for some reason feel frozen and unable to free myself from this thinking. like it always leads me to believe something is fundamentally wrong with me when i see so many people express themselves creatively so effortlessly regardless of medium, especially when said person is also someone who does computer stuff and is somehow able to be skilled in two totally at-odds modes of thought so i guess the crux of my question is how do i let go of this? or am i doomed? if i were a 6 year old child with absolutely no care for anything, it would be so easy
answ: there's a lot to unpack here. you have very severe self-doubt built into you. this condition is of course common among artists, but it's something you probably just have to live with, for the most part. it also gives you huge powers because you care such a huge amount. you also mention you might be "overthinking", but again that's probably a common condition for artists, and probably something you'll have to live with, AND again, also a tremendous asset for creativity. if you can survive the damage it does to you on the bad days. Next, i have to point out a giant leap of reasoning you made that i dont think is fair: you say "so many people express themselves creatively so effortlessly regardless of medium". i see no reason to assume that. the confusion and turmoil you've described in yourself is easily a standard level of turmoil that artists can go through. Can be less, can be even more, but your assumption that it's such a breeze for everyone, that's way off. it's way way way way off. sure, at the moment the best stuff happens, that is a magic moment miracle breeze, but this is not without 1000x more moments striving, stressing, doubting, etc. or just waiting patiently for the clouds to clear, as if by magic. Anyway, the point is you've done the thing where you've assumed that it's "so easy" for everyone else, it is certainly not, and in many many many cases it looks extremely similar to the struggles you've described in yourself. The next thing i must point out that i think is really interesting is, you say "am i doomed". The person who likes cake and doesnt get to eat cake might assume they are "doomed" if they cannot eat cake. The person who does not like cake and is forced to eat it might assume they are "doomed" if they are forced to eat cake. So when you contemplate being "doomed", just by saying what this means youve already spilled the beans on what you want here. you want to be an artist, and if you 'cant' then that would feel like a deep failure. Not everybody even wants to be an artist. and they certainly wouldnt consider it 'doom' if they couldnt be. So just the fact that you are here thinking youre doomed if you cant do art, that tells you everything you need to know about who you are, and in a broad sense there is no need to worry about not becoming who you are. it means everything to you and you'll do it just fine, in your own way. and you did not convince me that there are any show-stopping obstacles preventing it. just wholesome challenges that you'll probably even feel thankful for later

ques: i have a persistent issue with creating things: i will get a thing like 90% done, i.e. the point where i can say to myself "okay, i am mostly happy with this thing, i just need to clean it up a bit and add a little more spice before i can show it off to people", but then i just...don't do any of that, and i move on to making a brand new thing. the end result is a collection of things that make me Mostly happy but also vaguely guilty because i know i should be finishing them instead of making new things which i know i probably won't finish either. in my case the creating is just for fun so there is no external incentive to finish these things, but i would very much like to finish them regardless. is this an issue common among artists or am i just weird? and whether i am weird or normal, do you have any advice on Actually Finishing Things?
answ: if you want to finish them you should set a time limit on these 'finishings'. because the ideal amount of work remaining is actually very little. and in many cases the best choice is to just declare it finished as is. A funny thing about real audiences: they actually often enjoy it more if it's 10% unfinished. it lets them use their imagination more, and it keeps them paying attention. On the other hand, to hear something 100% 'done' often feels alienating to an audience. there's the feeling it doesnt really care about their input

ques: Hi Mr. Wurtz, I caught in a Scary Pockets track you were on that you use trad grip on the kit. I had to learn both but have always preferred matched. Exposing my bias, I'm a little down on trad because a lot of drumlines I've taught use it for the snares because it looks cool (which it does, admittedly), rather than thinking of the development of the student, where matched is more applicable to other instruments like the keys

or timpani. Do you use it because it's what's comfortable, do you switch between the two depending on the song, do you use it because it's cool (a good reason for any individual, but not for a teacher to use exclusively unless the students have the desire to learn it imo), or for some other purpose (and if so, what)? Also big props from a random stranger here, you're crazy in the pocket and the dryness of the kit on those tracks really accentuates that. And the ghost notes? The Groove? Don't even get me started. The reason I wanted to ask you, as opposed to an even more random stranger, is because I respect you as an accomplished and skilled drummer and would appreciate any insight you have!
answ: disagree. most instruments the hands do something different that compliment each other and its very romantic in that way, many people would argue

the origin was i think more practical than this, marching snares used to be slanted. But, my origin with it is totally random; basketball injury around age 10, then temporarily could not bend my left middle finger. so i switched. BUT, i was already hooked on dave weckl as a youngster and FOR SURE it looked cool, but i never had the motivation to switch (it's naturally weird at first). then that basketball fell on my finger, and i was like 'huh, i can still actually play if i switch to trad, might as well try it' and when my finger got better (maybe a week later?), as they say....... "you never go back." (well at least a lot of people say that). Ok but so, as far as "which one is better", i will firmly stand behind freedom of choice. you'll be just fine either way. matched is totally good, it obviously makes sense, trad was created for obsolete technical circumstances, so it makes perfect sense that that one will fade away. BUT, here's the funny thing..... if you ask around, it always seems like everyone who does use trad grip........ LOVES it, and they say it's so much more inspiring and feels much more elegant to have your hands doing different things, and it feels like the hands are responding to one another 'organically'. people really fall in love with traditional grip. Like the manual stick-shifter in an car, this really seems to be one of those "never go back" things. it's something people really fall in love with

ques: how do i get better at writing chord progressions?
answ: what do you think the chords are about? Hint: sing the words and melody, or, if it's for a filmscore, watch the scenes. if neither of those things exist yet, then usually dont do the chords first. Or if you do, dont think of "writing chords" when there's no melody words or scene yet. sure you can start with some chords, but only insofar as it gets you in the mood to start writing the actual thing youre writing (the words/melody/scene, what happens). Because without that, the chords will be complaining to you that their existence is meaningless. Chords are there to inject emotion subliminally into things. Without any 'thing' there to inject emotion into, chords cant even do their job. Like a hypnotizer beam with no one to hypnotize. I mean this is like at the dinner table, when you salt your plate first, and cant figure out which way to do it. salt the food not the plate. are you getting it

ques: i've been trying to use your factoring method. i'm doing well on a number i was given online, but when i added 39 to turn 3471 into 3510, and killed the zero, i then got 13x27, which is taking me further. i couldn't find in the note you made that has the intructions on how to factor a number what to do if that works, since you ended up with a prime number. whats the deal?
answ: i'd say i think you missed 3. you start by checking 2, then 3, then 5, then 7 etc. and when you get a hit, divide it out. so in this case you'd divide the 3471 by 3, get 1157, check 3 again (you always have to check the same factor again after a hit because it could have multiple, but you never have to check past factors again). so then you continue on to check 7, 11, etc. Then you'd hit with 13, you'd have seen that probably by adding 13 to get to 1170, so 117, and you'd hit it that way. so 13 is in. Then you divide the 13 out, 1157 div by 13 is 89, and now 89 is the new 'big number' to continue with, or to be your answer, depending on your level of experience. theoretically if you didnt know 89 you would continue, i guess you'd have to check 13 again. but you actually dont anyway because 13 squared is already way bigger but if you knew that then you probably also knew 89 was prime anyway. but anyway, so then you just have to collect your results to get the primefactorization of the original number. 89x13x3

ques: 11.13.25 2:08 pm I may have botched that transcription (and it is transcription, I'm making music, not theory). I promise I'm not in it for the chord symbols, not in the slightest. You kinda roasted me there re: the sounds the symbols represent, but it's okay, I forgive you. My songwriting intuition is somewhat worse off for my exposing myself to music that makes poor songwriting decisions that, while they still work, feel unsatisfying. You seem to have a good intuition for what feels musically satisfying, so I ask you again: C Cmaj7 Cmaj7/F Bbadd9/F Dmin9 Fmaj7/G G9 Gmin7 Gmin9no5 C13no3no5no11 C11no3 Dbadd4 Db7add#4 ____. What are my best options?
answ: let me see if i can explain what i'm seeing here........ imagine if someone said to you, "Here is my picture so far: green, green, blue, yellow, green, purple, green ________. what is the next color that would be best for the picture"? Even if i understand color-words perfectly, i'm still not going to have any idea what's in the picture, AND, even further, i wouldnt even know what the colors really are! because the names are never accurate enough to express the colors. but more importantly i still can't see the picture. Another analogy, someone says can you help me with my programming code, here i'll tell you the last word of each line. what to you think the last word of the next line should be. It's possible that your songwriting method differs from mine, in all fairness, but 'only chords' for me is a 1-way ticket to emptiness. and i say this even as a person who is way chord-crazy, chords are like the absolute best thing for this world, but they do absolutely nothing for me unless they are activated by melodies, words, and scenes. In the rare case where just chords are enough, then it even more is all gonna come down to the SOUND. which is not shown at all in a chord list, any more than a list of colors can represent a visual depiction of color. my best concise honest answer for the "what comes next in this chord list" is, as you know, drawing attention to the word/melody department. but you specifically requested that i not do that. so that's why i started to think you are really hangin on a little too tightly to these chords. seriously, for me normally on a writing session, it's a general rule of thumb let's say i wanna know, at any given moment, "why has this run out of gas right here"...... and i always check and yep, sure enough, it's because the chord/melody departent has gotten, even just 3 SECONDS... ahead of the words. the whole thing just becomes meaningless right there. And this is chord AND melody, and it STILL runs out of gas if the chord+mel gets ahead of the words for even just a couple seconds. what i'm saying is it would be even more extreme if JUST the chords got ahead. you'd be dead. (or at least i would). so for me this idea of writing "just the chords" is just one of those things that like..... doesnt work for me at all. again it's ironic that i say this because chords to me are perhaps one of the most cherished things in my tool kit. but they do ABSOLUTELY NOTHING out of context of melody at the very least, but stronger still the words OR in some cases this may be scenes, or whatever context this music is living in. salting the plate analogy, the eating pure msg analogy, i could hammer these analogies all day but you actually told me i shouldn't tell you to add words. so i was like, ok, maybe it really is about the chord list, so that's when i started looking into aesthetic options for doing things with the chord symbols, because you seemed pretty attached to those being the main thing at play here. 'if you cant beatem joinem' was sort of how i was feeling
